items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Steven Spielberg’s L.A. Ranch Sells for $8 Million Below Asking—Just Two Months After Hitting the Market
items.summary:
Filmmaker Steven Spielberg has sold the sprawling Los Angeles ranch where he housed his horses for $22.3 million—just two months after listing the palatial pad. 

Spielberg, 79, and his wife, Kate Capshaw , 72, purchased the property in 1999 through their corporate entity, Texas Tart, for $5.75 million.

They then listed the massive compound in September for $30 million. Then, in late October, the home disappeared from the market, with no indication as to why. 

Now, Realtor.com® can exclusively reveal that the property has traded hands, selling for $22.3 million—a nearly $8 million discount from its initial asking price.

When they purchased the home, the Hollywood mogul and actress unveiled ambitious plans to dramatically overhaul the estate with a 27,000-square-foot, five-story riding facility featuring a domed roof and underground horse stables.

Spielberg's vision also reportedly included more than $7 million worth of renovations, as well as plans to construct a 2,400-square-foot guesthouse and a three-story guardhouse.

Filmmaker Steven Spielberg has sold the sprawling Los Angeles ranch where he housed his horses for $22.3 million—just two months after listing the palatial pad. (Presley Ann/Getty Images for Lucas Museum of Narrative Art) 

However, the proposed transformation sparked fierce backlash from neighbors, who objected to the scale of the project.

Although the Oscar-winning director reportedly planned to present revised ideas to his neighbors, the elaborate project ultimately never came to fruition. However, he did get a chance to update the estate into the…
items.t: EXCLUSIVE: Steven Spielberg’s L.A. Ranch Sells for $8 Million Below Asking—Just Two Months After Hitting the Market

items.title: Jensen Huang is Reinstated as Nvidia CEO
items.summary:
Nvidia board of directors announced Monday that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as company president and CEO less than two weeks after his resignation over extramarital affairs. 

The board said in a statement that it voted unanimously to bring back Huang effective immediately after holding a series of meetings and discussions with the ousted executive that convinced board members of his "candor and ability to lead Nvidia." 

The announcement noted that the Nvidia board received input from "from senior levels of the United States government" that left it confident that Huang’s reinstatement "poses no national security risk". 

Huang, 63, voluntarily stepped down on Nov. 12 amid reports of multiple dalliances, including one with foreign business executive and suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang , and another with Nvidia healthcare executive Kimberly Powell , who was his direct subordinate.  

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," said Nvidia Board Chair Harvey C. Jones . "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company."

This marks a sharp U-turn for Jones, who said on an earnings call last week that the board had no intention of reinstating Huang. 

In a statement, Huang said in part that he is honored to return to Nvidia and is thankful to the board for its confidence, and to the employees, shareholders, and his family for thier support. 

"I take this responsibility with the…
items.t: Jensen Huang is Reinstated as Nvidia CEO

items.title: Young Adults Living With Parents Surge Fastest in America’s Once-Affordable Regions
items.summary:
Young adults living with their parents have become a familiar symbol of America's housing affordability crisis . But the geography of that living arrangement is changing, according to new research.

A record 25.2 million Americans aged 18 to 34 lived with their parents in 2025, or roughly 1 in 3 young adults. Nationally, that share barely budged between the pooled 2020–22 and 2023–25 periods, according to The Geography of the Crowded Nest , a new report from Realtor.com® .

Beneath that apparent stability, however, the South and Midwest—long considered the nation's affordability havens—recorded the largest year-over-year increases in 2025, with the share living at home rising 1.4 percentage points to 32.3% and 31.7%, respectively.

Meanwhile, in the notoriously expensive Northeast—where living with parents has historically been most common—the rate fell 2.3 percentage points to 36.9%, its lowest level since 2010.

It pushes back against conventional logic that cheaper housing markets offer young adults an easier path to independence.

"This is not a coastal problem that has stayed coastal; it has spread to even the more-accessible parts of the country," writes Hannah Jones , senior economist at Realtor.com and author of the report .

Perhaps the clearest illustration comes from two metros that, at first glance, seem worlds apart: San Antonio, TX, and Boston, MA .

One is steeped in cowboy culture; the other, Ivy League academia. In October, the median asking rent in Boston was $2,954, more than double the $1,117 in San Antonio. Yet the share of young adults living with…
items.t: Young Adults Living With Parents Surge Fastest in America’s Once-Affordable Regions

items.title: Asking Mom and Dad for Down Payment Help This Thanksgiving? Here’s How Much To Ask For
items.summary:
Thanksgiving . A time for turkey, football, and the gathering of family. 

It can be a stressful day for many, from the demands of traveling to the obligations of hosting at home . But hopefully, for most, it’s a day to be spent being thankful for having the loved ones gathered around the table. 

And what better time to ask those loved ones for a bit of help to achieve the American dream than on a quintessential American holiday?

Jokes aside, if it’s on your holiday agenda to hit up Mom, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa, or even cool Aunt Janet for some money to buy a home next year, there’s a few things you should know before making the trip.

Like how much you’re actually going to need for that dream home. 

A helping hand 

The reality is, young people really do need help with down payments these days—and many are getting it. 

In the past year, 25% of first-time homebuyers used gifts or loans from family and friends to help fund their down payment, according to the National Association of Realtors® 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers .

Furthermore, whether they’re going it alone or with help, all buyers are strapped for the cash for down payments as overall payments are on the decline. 

The typical down payment share dropped for four straight quarters, softening to 12.8% in the first quarter of 2026, down 1.1 percentage points from a year earlier, according to the most recent Realtor.com® down payment report . 

In dollar terms, down payments sank 19% year over year to their lowest point since the third quarter of 2021.

Be grateful for the ones you love this…
items.t: Asking Mom and Dad for Down Payment Help This Thanksgiving? Here’s How Much To Ask For

items.title: President Woodrow Wilson’s Historic Princeton Home Lists for $5.85 Million After a 7-Year Restoration
items.summary:
The home where Woodrow Wilson lived as a professor before becoming president has hit the market in Princeton, NJ for $5.85 million.

The Tudor Revival at 82 Library Place was built in 1896 for Wilson and he lived there with his wife, Ellen, and their three children until 1902, when he became president of Princeton University and moved on campus. 

The home was first listed in May 2025 for $6.5 million. 

“Wilson and his wife had a lot of input in the design and finishes chosen for the home, which included double stained-glass doors from the Sears catalog,” says listing agent Barbara Blackwell of Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty .

The backyard comes with garden-lined patios and a koi pond (Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty) 

The home underwent a seven year top-to-bottom restoration (Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty) 

Inside the new sunroom (Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty) 

The estate is one of only two working homes in the U.S. designed and built by a president, the other being Monticello, according to the listing. 

Blackwell says the house has had 19 owners since the Wilsons, including Princeton University itself, which used the home as faculty housing during the Great Depression.

The current owners spent seven years restoring the property with architect Ron Berlin and Baxter Construction. The award-winning project brought back the original beams and woodwork and re-glassed the leaded windows. It also gave the home a distinct sense of presidential charm, making it easy to imagine Wilson tucked among…
items.t: President Woodrow Wilson’s Historic Princeton Home Lists for $5.85 Million After a 7-Year Restoration

Built in 1899, the five-bedroom residence underwent a “no-expense-spared” reconstruction and features 13 newly renovated rooms, each with individually zoned heating and cooling.

The six-story dwelling features a garden level that leads to a limestone gallery with custom paneling. French doors open to a bluestone-decked garden with a built-in grill.

items.title: Inside a Secluded Cabin Hidden Right Beneath Big Sur’s Iconic Landmark
items.summary:
A secluded retreat tucked beneath one of California’s most photographed landmarks in Big Sur has come on the market for $3.65 million.

The home at 39320 Coast Road sits in Bixby Canyon and is one of only seven residences behind a private gate.

“Millions recognize Bixby Bridge, yet very few will ever experience the landscape beneath it,” says listing agent Michael Hornig of the Strock Team at eXp Realty .

The entrance of the cabin, which is one of only seven properties in the canyon. (Lost Coast Media) 

The main room and kitchen (Lost Coast Media) 

A cozy living room (Lost Coast Media) 

The canyon also comes with a literary history: In 1960, Jack Kerouac retreated to a cabin here owned by Lawrence Ferlinghetti , the poet and co-founder of City Lights Bookstore. His time in the canyon formed the basis for his 1962 novel, “Big Sur.” While this is not the original Kerouac cabin, it shares the same setting.

According to Hornig, the canyon has also been home to the film director Sam Peckinpah and the Disney illustrator Ron Dias. 

“There’s an extraordinary feeling about this canyon,” Hornig says. “You’re surrounded by a landscape that inspired some of America’s most influential writers, and remarkably, much of that atmosphere of solitude and wilderness remains intact today.”

Built in 1984, the single-level home has three bedrooms, two full bathrooms, and 1,489 square feet of living space. Vaulted, open-beam ceilings, hardwood floors, and three wood-burning stoves characterize the interiors, as do large windows that frame the surrounding redwoods. A wraparound porch…
items.t: Inside a Secluded Cabin Hidden Right Beneath Big Sur’s Iconic Landmark

items.title: New Development in the Heart of Florida Equestrian Country Targets Horse Lovers With Farm Lots and Bridle Paths
items.summary:
A new masterplanned community in the heart of Palm Beach County's equestrian country has opened sales to wealthy horse lovers.

The Wellington , a private club community in the Village of Wellington , sitting about 16 miles east of West Palm Beach, will cater to the horsey set.

The 253-unit masterplanned community—with estate homes starting at $11 million and townhomes at $6.8 million—will also feature an 18-hole link-style championship golf course designed by Scottish golf course architect David McLay Kidd . The median list price in the surrounding area is $849,900, a 12% increase over last year.

But the new community will distinguish itself from the luxury development pack with high-end equestrian villas and farm lots, along with a bridle path connecting to the premiere equestrian venue, Wellington International Showgrounds.

Developer Wellington Lifestyle Partners poured capital into improving the show grounds, adding 100 acres and erecting new competition rings, a covered riding arena, a grass derby field, and stabling that's designed to prioritize ventilation, horse welfare, and rider comfort.

The improvements are expected to encourage exhibitors to arrive earlier in the fall and stay longer into the spring and summer, reinforcing the village's equestrian ecosystem, which pumps about $600 million annually into the local economy, according to the county .

items.title: Inside OldWalls: A Famous Sculptor’s $4.15 Million Stone Compound 55 Miles From New York City
items.summary:
California-born sculptor Chester Beach worked out of a New York City studio between 1907 and 1952, nabbing high-profile commissions from the Panama-Pacific International Exposition, as well as the 1928 Summer Olympics.

But, like many artists, he carved out space for a pastoral retreat away from the hustle and bustle. 

In 1917, after living in Rome for a brief period, he and his wife, Eleanor Beach , established a home in Brewster, NY , in Putnam County, just 55 miles north of the city. They named the Arts & Crafts-style estate OldWalls.

Now these 10.49 acres—including four buildings, comprising a compound—is looking for a new steward. 

"There have only been three owners including the original family that owned it up until 2009," says listing agent Will Stuart, of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices New England Properties . "My sellers have been there for two years."

The historic estate spans 10.49 acres and includesfour buildings. (Realtor.com) 

The estate has formal gardens, stone patios and multiple porches and terraces. (Realtor.com) 

The stone home features plaster walls and wood detailing. Pictured is the living room, with a fireplace. (Realtor.com) 

Listing for $4,150,000, the new owner won't be the first to seek a deeper connection to nature while still being close to Manhattan. 

Stuart notes that this eight-bedroom, 6.5-bath spread is exceptionally tied to its origins. 

"Each owner has become a steward of the property and has preserved extensive family photographs, memoirs and documents, and have really kept the story going, which is rare with these kinds of…
items.t: Inside OldWalls: A Famous Sculptor’s $4.15 Million Stone Compound 55 Miles From New York City

items.title: How an Artsy Pennsylvania River Town Became an Architectural Powerhouse Where Old Meets New
items.summary:
At first glance, New Hope, PA , looks like little more than a picturesque, upscale river town with a vibrant arts scene. However, a closer look reveals that the historic borough shares an architectural DNA with Europe's premier capitals.

Located halfway between New York City and Philadelphia , New Hope spans roughly 1.42 square miles and is home to fewer than 3,000 year-round residents. Yet it boasts an outsized reputation as a beloved regional tourist destination renowned for its art galleries, boutiques, riverside dining, and cultural institutions, led by the iconic Bucks County Playhouse , which has hosted major stars such as Grace Kelly , Robert Redford , and Liza Minnelli. 

In New Hope's luxury housing market, old and new blend seamlessly: 18th-century structures are brought into the 21st century with bold, modern additions and amenities.

"A lot of the homes around here, especially some of the larger homes, all started off as an old stone farmhouse, so incorporating some of that character while building the big steel and glass additions is very much an architectural vibe that is done here," Nicholas Esser , managing partner at Addison Wolfe Real Estate , tells Realtor.com® .

The market's remarkably varied housing stock also includes stately Colonial and Victorian homes, sprawling legacy estates, and cutting-edge new construction that would not look out of place in the heart of Silicon Valley.

Architect Ralph Fey , with Ralph C. Fey Architects in Doylestown, PA , explains that New Hope's signature look is rooted in regulatory necessity, because more than half of…
items.t: How an Artsy Pennsylvania River Town Became an Architectural Powerhouse Where Old Meets New

items.title: New York’s Luxury Rental Market Sees Influx of Cash from AI Boom
items.summary:
The artificial intelligence boom has expanded from the rolling hills of San Francisco and Silicon Valley to the busy streets of New York City, where an already tight luxury market is feeling the impact.

The AI wealth boom was in the spotlight this week, following Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO and jaw dropping $1.494 trillion valuation. With the tech constantly growing and producing newly minted millionaires, the impacts of deep-pocketed AI professionals entering the New York real estate market are just beginning to be felt, agents there say.

There are more than 2,000 AI companies operating in New York City, according to the city’s Economic Development Corporation , and AI companies signed leases for about 1.5 million square feet in just the first six months of 2026, the Brooklyn Daily Eagle reported.

Major AI frontrunners like Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI, and EliseAI have opened offices in New York, contributing to the thriving commercial real estate market.

“It’s been pretty unbelievable, what’s happening in the public sphere of the AI business. We’re seeing a ton of AI leasing activity on the ground in New York,” Evan Kleinberg , co-founder of Cornelia Street Partners , a boutique commercial real estate firm, told Realtor.com. “And it’s been happening so fast, it’s almost representative of the technology itself. The companies hire immediately and they need space yesterday.”

While Kleinberg has been keeping eyes on the AI industry for the past couple of years, his brokerage worked with its first AI specific company about 12 months ago, at the end of 2025. Since…
items.t: New York’s Luxury Rental Market Sees Influx of Cash from AI Boom

items.title: The Rise of the House Manager: Why Busy Families Are Outsourcing Everyday Tasks
items.summary:
Between managing the demands of work and keeping up with everything at home, it can feel like there are never enough hours in the day. 

For busy, overscheduled families, hiring a house manager may be the key to reclaiming valuable time, reducing daily stress, and bringing a little more balance to everyday life.

For those who are unfamiliar with this trending form of home support, a house manager is basically someone who keeps track of things behind the scenes so you can off-load some of your never-ending to-do list.

"A house manager takes on the parts of the household a family chooses to hand off—that means both the everyday work and the planning behind it, from start to finish," says Kelly Hubbell , founder and CEO of Sage Haus , a thriving house manager placement company. "Think meals, laundry, errands, calendars, pet care, and home projects. A house manager doesn't just complete tasks ... they anticipate what's needed and handle it without being asked."

In other words, a house manager is an added support system that helps keep a household functioning efficiently. 

Hiring a house manager allowed Kelly Hubbell more time with her family and led to her building a company to help others do the same. (Lion & Oak Photography) 

What exactly is a house manager and what do they do? 

The simplest definition of a house manger is someone who helps facilitate everyday life behind the scenes.

"A housekeeper cleans, a nanny cares for the kids, a house manager owns whole areas of the household, from planning to follow-through," says Hubbell.

There can be overlap. A house…
items.t: The Rise of the House Manager: Why Busy Families Are Outsourcing Everyday Tasks

items.title: Melania Trump Shares Rare Details on Her White House Renovations and Design Plans in ‘Melania: The Series’
items.summary:
Melania Trump has given another look into her life as first lady with the premiere of “Melania: The Series,” a two-episode follow-up to the previously released "Melania" documentary .

Both the film and the series detail the weeks leading up to President Donald Trump ’s January 2025 inauguration .

In the first episode, which was released on Nov. 20, Melania prepares to resume her White House duties for a second term.

“The role of the first lady is managing of the White House,” she explained. “And I think people don’t realize that the first lady is in charge of the residence.”

She spoke at length about her approach to the role, noting the pride she takes in carrying out duties such as decorating the Washington, DC , landmark and planning events.

A new two-part documentary, "Melania: The Series," has premiered, detailing the first lady's preparation to return to the White House before the 2025 inauguration. (Photo by Stephanie Augello/Getty Images)

items.title: Traveling Home for Thanksgiving? How Smart Buyers Turn Holiday Visits Into Neighborhood Recon
items.summary:
For most people, family is everything.

That’s why it’s no surprise that the latest Migration Trends report by the National Association of Realtors® found that 30% of buyers who relocated did so to be near family. 

Whether the goal is to care for aging parents , assist with childcare , or simply enjoy more time with loved ones, living near family can make a positive difference in everyday life.

If you’ve been contemplating buying a home closer to family, your Thanksgiving visit could be the perfect opportunity to start exploring what life in a new area could look like. 

Since you’re already making the trip, it only makes sense to get a firsthand look at the neighborhoods, homes, and local amenities to help you determine whether the move is worthwhile for your budget and lifestyle.

“Seeing how a community operates when people are home, traffic is heavier, and daily routines are stressed can help you make an informed decision about where to plant roots,” says Cameron Walker , real estate expert and manager of the agent network at Clever Real Estate in St. Louis .

How to turn your Thanksgiving trip into a test-drive 

Once you arrive in town for Thanksgiving, take a commute during rush hour. 

Then, walk around the area during the day and at night and check out local shops, restaurants, parks, and other attractions.

“Be sure to speak to locals about traffic, parking, safety, noise, and other concerns that might arise during different seasons,” says Walker.

Pay attention to all the small details that will matter if you make the move: sidewalk length and quality, road…
items.t: Traveling Home for Thanksgiving? How Smart Buyers Turn Holiday Visits Into Neighborhood Recon

items.title: Drought-Stricken Nevada Town Erupts Over Luxury Development’s Plan for ‘Firefighter Pond’
items.summary:
Should a private developer have the ability to build a human-made pond in the middle of a drought-stricken region? What if that developer says that firefighters can access the pond to fight wildfires? 

That’s the question at the center of a growing debate in Clark County, NV , where water is scarce and locals are skeptical about a luxury development's plan to create a massive water feature. 

Joel Laub and his partner, Randall Jones , began developing the Reserve at Red Rock Canyon in 2022, aiming to create a high-end luxury community amid the Nevada wilderness. The Reserve is being built on 65 acres that were once home to the Bonnie Springs Ranch, a historic, Old West-themed family resort that once featured horseback riding and a small zoo. 

Two-acre empty plots in the community start at $7.5 million. But that’s not what has the community up in arms. Instead, it’s what the Reserve is touting on its website: a large human-made pond in the middle of the property. 

To outsiders, it seems like just one feature in a long list of amenities. But for some locals in Clark County, which was declared a natural disaster area due to drought earlier this year, the pond seems like a slap in the face—even as the developers attempt to position it as a fire safety "dip pond."

“This little dip pond here is really fire safety as an afterthought, and I think that’s pretty obvious in terms of even their planning,” said Sarah J. McCrea-Dameron , a Blue Diamond, NV, resident and former deputy fire chief from Las Vegas Fire & Rescue, at a zoning commission meeting this past week. “It’s not in…
items.t: Luxury Developer Says He’s Building a Pond in Drought-Stricken Area To Fight Fires. Critics Don’t Believe Him.

items.title: Their HOA Approved Their Backyard Fences. Now They’re Being Told To Tear Them Down.
items.summary:
Almost six years ago, Laura Burns-Sierra hired Home Depot to install a fence around her property in the Cypress Mill community near Tampa, FL . She submitted the plans to her homeowners association, received written approval and had the fence professionally installed.

Now, another organization says the fence has to come down.

"We couldn't do anything, any construction, any fences, nothing, without HOA approval," Burns-Sierra tells Realtor.com® . "I followed the procedures to the T."

Burns-Sierra is among a group of homeowners in the Sun City Center neighborhood caught in an unusual dispute between their HOA and the Cypress Mill Community Development District , or CDD. The latter says fences installed within drainage easements are interfering with its ability to maintain the community's stormwater infrastructure and now need to be removed.

Stormwater ponds sit behind rows of homes in the Cypress Mill community in Sun City Center, FL. (Google Earth) 

The conflict has left residents facing hundreds or even thousands of dollars in unexpected expenses—and raises an important question for homeowners everywhere:

Is an HOA's written approval enough to protect you when another governing body has authority over your property?

2 organizations, 2 sets of rules 

At the center of the dispute is a distinction many homeowners may not realize exists.

An HOA generally oversees community standards, including architectural approvals, landscaping, and fence design. A CDD, meanwhile, is a special-purpose local government that can be responsible for infrastructure such as roads,…
items.t: Their HOA Approved Their Backyard Fences. Now They’re Being Told To Tear Them Down.

items.title: Dow and S&P 500 Plunge Into Correction as Tech Sell-Off Deepens
items.summary:
The major stock indexes extended their losses on Friday, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 briefly plunged into correction territory, defined as a 10% decline from their last peak.

By the closing bell, the S&P 500 had fallen 265 points, or 3.70%, while the Dow Jones dropped 949 points, or 1.93%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite tumbled 5.28%, wiping out its gains for the year.

The sell-off, driven by a wipeout in tech and AI stocks, comes a day after Anthropic raised a staggering $81.34 billion during its IPO on Thursday, lifting the company's valuation to $1.414 trillion.

Anthropic shares were down 12% on Friday, giving back most of their gains after jumping 17% in their debut session.

Sevens Report Research's Tom Essaye said Thursday's sell-off primarily hit the tech sector, but added that "weakness is extending this morning and, like yesterday, pulling the broad market lower (although there was no new negative news overnight in the tech sector)."

Housing stocks—especially those of major homebuilders—have shown relative strength this month due to continued institutional investment from firms such as Berkshire Hathaway. (Stock photo) (Getty Images) 

Concerns over inflation, a potential U.S. government shutdown in December, and continued conflict in the Middle East have kept some investors on edge. That, coupled with a recent spate of tech outages—including the FAA outage last Friday and the Microsoft outage last Thursday—have created a sense of unease among tech investors.

AI investors were already feeling wary—as the burgeoning AI industry matures, it…
items.t: Dow and S&P 500 Plunge Into Correction as Tech Selloff Deepens

Housing minister hails ‘historic moment’ as he publishes bill to eventually ban almost all new leasehold properties

Leaseholders in England and Wales will have their ground rent capped in 2028, the housing minister has said as he publishes a bill that will eventually ban virtually all new leasehold properties.

Matthew Pennycook will introduce the government’s leasehold reform bill on Thursday, including measures to cap charges, end the sale of new leasehold flats and make it easier to extend and buy out leases.
